request: the job state file save path and its exit codes

defects.description: saveState opens the live state file with 'w', which truncates it, and writes in place; a write that fails or a crash part-way leaves a truncated file that loadState rejects, losing every recorded job instead of keeping the previous state.

trigger.input: saveState(f,{jobs:{a:'done'}}); recordJob(f,'b','running', fs) where fs.writeSync writes the first 10 bytes then throws ENOSPC; then loadState(f)
trigger.expected: the save throws and loadState(f) returns {"jobs":{"a":"done"}} (previous state intact)
trigger.actual: save threw ENOSPC; file content is "{\n  \"jobs\""; load: SyntaxError: Expected ':' after property name in JSON at position 10 (line 2 column 9)

defects.why_missed: The suite only saves to a healthy temp directory and reads back, so no test makes a write fail part-way or looks at the file after an interrupted save.
defects.severity_rationale: A write failure or crash during replacement can destroy previously persisted jobs under that specific failure condition.
defects.expected_behavior: the save throws and loadState(f) returns {"jobs":{"a":"done"}} (previous state intact)
defects.failure_condition: saveState(f,{jobs:{a:'done'}}); recordJob(f,'b','running', fs) where fs.writeSync writes the first 10 bytes then throws ENOSPC; then loadState(f) -> save threw ENOSPC; file content is "{\n  \"jobs\""; load: SyntaxError: Expected ':' after property name in JSON at position 10 (line 2 column 9)

detection_criteria.mechanism: saveState opens the live state file with 'w', which truncates it, and writes in place; a write that fails or a crash part-way leaves a truncated file that loadState rejects, losing every recorded job instead of keeping the previous state.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the record lost, duplicated or corrupted, and the operation sequence that does it.

defects.description: The mark command catches a failed save, prints a warning and still returns 0, so a scheduler is told the job was recorded when the state file was not written.

trigger.input: run(['mark','b','done'], {fs, env:{JOB_STATE_FILE:f}, err, out}) where fs.writeSync throws ENOSPC
trigger.expected: exit code 1 (README: 1 when the state could not be saved)
trigger.actual: exit 0, stderr "warning: could not save state: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write\n"

defects.why_missed: Every CLI test runs against a writable file, so the catch branch never executes and no test asserts the exit code of a failed save.
defects.severity_rationale: A failed disk write is reported as success after an I/O error, leaving state unrecorded under that failure condition.
defects.expected_behavior: exit code 1 (README: 1 when the state could not be saved)
defects.failure_condition: run(['mark','b','done'], {fs, env:{JOB_STATE_FILE:f}, err, out}) where fs.writeSync throws ENOSPC -> exit 0, stderr "warning: could not save state: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write\n"

detection_criteria.mechanism: The mark command catches a failed save, prints a warning and still returns 0, so a scheduler is told the job was recorded when the state file was not written.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the injected fault, the expected degradation, and the observed wrong behaviour.
